diagnosis: The scenario fails the Weak Arm gate because several checks are satisfied by generic model behavior or default assumptions. Specifically, C4 (linked to PF2) passed in all rollouts, likely due to the model defaulting to 'false' for training permission as a safety heuristic. Additionally, C8 and C9 (linked to PF4) passed in rollout 2 despite the agent having no access to PF4, suggesting the model is pattern-matching the need for compliance/audits when it sees a 'DENIED' launch decision.

C4.why: The standard privacy template permits ordinary product-improvement use and does not set the partner's timing, while PF2 changes the terms to prohibit model training and require deletion exactly 30 days after termination.

C8.why: The standard enterprise draft contains neither the anchor hospital's production prerequisite nor its governance right, while PF4 changes it to require a SOC 2 Type II report before production and an annual customer audit right.

C9.why: The standard enterprise draft contains neither the anchor hospital's production prerequisite nor its governance right, while PF4 changes it to require a SOC 2 Type II report before production and an annual customer audit right.
